body.x: WITZ Inc. (CEO Park JinIk) has announced its participation in CES 2025, taking place from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, where it will introduce its innovative IP licensing platform, “WitzShop,” at the “K-Startup Pavilion.”

Founded to simplify the traditional complexities of the licensing market, WITZ aims to create an environment where licensing agreements are accessible and secure for everyone. Its flagship platform, WitzShop, supports seamless licensing transactions while leveraging AI-powered counterfeit detection technology, WitzGuard, to protect users’ intellectual property (IP).

Recognized for its innovation in digitizing IP licensing, WITZ plans to expand its global client base by highlighting WitzShop’s capabilities at CES 2025. The platform efficiently connects IP owners with potential buyers and ensures that AI-generated content IP can be used legally and effectively. As generative AI continues to proliferate across the global tech landscape, WitzShop addresses the need for transparency and growth within this evolving market.

WitzShop simplifies cross-border IP licensing by clearly defining ownership and rights, strengthening the safety and efficiency of international IP transactions. Following royalty payments, the platform automatically generates standardized contracts, which legal experts review, reducing the risk of disputes. Additionally, the time required for contract completion after payment has been significantly reduced to two to three days, enhancing convenience for sellers and buyers.

With an intuitive interface and user-friendly design, WitzShop caters to licensing professionals and beginners, earning praise for its accessibility and streamlined processes. “WitzShop is a one-stop platform that fully digitizes and automates the IP licensing process, minimizing spatial and temporal constraints,” said a company representative. “By transparently disclosing transaction conditions and using verification technology to ensure IP integrity, we expect strong demand for our solution globally.”

At CES 2025, WITZ aims to elevate the brand value of WitzShop and explore its potential in overseas markets. The company also plans to establish networks with North American creators and facilitate the export of their IPs to high-demand regions like China and Southeast Asia, focusing on building a global licensing ecosystem.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
